title: haea how-to (long)
note: Script: docs/video/haea-howto-script.md. Footage: simulator, demo data only.

scenes.narration: This is haea, an iPhone app from Purplelink that reads Apple Health and gives you a daily readiness briefing. All of the analysis runs on the iPhone. Everything on screen in this video is demo data.
The Today tab opens with the briefing: a readiness score, a short headline, and one suggestion for the day. Here the score is sixty-four, and the suggestion is a twenty-minute walk.
Below that, a warning shows up only when something stands out, like sleep debt over the last five nights. Today's health shows sleep, movement, recovery and fuel, each with a seven-day trend.

haea gets this from Apple Health: sleep, heart rate, heart rate variability, workouts and weight. You choose what to allow. It reads nutrition that other apps write there, and it doesn't log food itself.
The Strength tab is your workout log. Tap Start workout, then choose one of your own routines or a program.
It shows weekly volume by muscle, personal records with estimated one-rep maxes, and your strength level against population standards. A deload check watches your fatigue.
The Running tab tracks runs on iPhone or Apple Watch. It suggests runs for the week, and shows training load, weekly distance and personal records.
To plan a route, tap points on the map. haea can follow paths between them, using Apple Maps, and shows the distance as you go. Then you can follow the route on a run.
Insights asks one question: what moves your sleep, running pace, weight or mood? Pick an outcome, and haea ranks your habits by how strongly each one is linked, using your own data.
A link isn't proof that one thing causes another. To check one, tap Try a small test, and change a single habit.
The Coach tab answers questions about your training. It uses Apple Intelligence on the device, on iPhones that support it.
haea has no account, no cloud sync, no ads and no tracking. Your records stay in a database on the iPhone.
haea is for general wellness. It is not medical advice, and it doesn't diagnose or treat anything. For medical questions, talk to a doctor.
haea is free to download. The briefing, strength log and running work without paying. An optional Premium subscription adds deeper analysis. The options are in the description.
haea. Your Apple Health data, analyzed on your iPhone.
